quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlight during the day.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and correct lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may cause poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel; lane markings; steel plates; and utility hole covers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: The best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight and running lights on. Use your high beam during the day and night when it is safe and legal to do so. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When you start your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Make sure your motorcycle is in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that shows when the engine is on and in neutral.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: A change in road surface coming up
Conditions that do not change as you get closer

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that do not change as you get closer
questions.explanation: Look for problems on the road and make a plan to stay safe.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake can prevent you from learning to use the front brake correctly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle more space and proceed carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's brakes work.

questions.question: You can be seen more easily at an intersection by:
questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times helps other drivers see you at intersections.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle and must ride over it, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil is low. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and is operated by the rider's left foot.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: So you can be seen in the vehicle's side mirror.
So you can be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
So you can be seen through the vehicle's passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself behind and in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror, where most drivers look more often than at side mirrors.

questions.question: What should riders know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are nothing to worry about.
They don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when appropriate, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: The center lane position places you in the driver's rearview mirror, making you most visible. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.

questions.question: How do reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing help riders?

options.text: They should only be worn at night.
They help other drivers see you better.
They do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Brightly-colored or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: A plastic face shield can protect you from:
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects you from rocks, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects. It also protects your face if you crash.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes of drinking it and affects your riding ability right away. Riding while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked. This helps you stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake pressure right away. Then apply the brake again with steady, gentle pressure.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Cross into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.
